sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your Twenties, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your Twenties》，在这个播客里，我们探讨20多岁时经历的一些重大人生变化和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, It is so great to have you here back for another episode,
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你在世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，

sentences.en: back for another topic as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 回来探讨另一个话题，让我们一起剖析20多岁的心理。

sentences.en: When we think about our 20s, I think there are four things that we worry about more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 当我们想到20多岁时，我认为有四件事是我们最担心的。

sentences.en: We worry about love, we worry about money, the future, and finally, our friendships.
sentences.zh: 我们担心爱情、金钱、未来，最后是我们的友谊。

sentences.en: Today, we're really going to focus in on that final point there and examine the way that our friendships change during this decade
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将重点关注最后一点，审视我们的友谊在这个十年里是如何变化的，

sentences.en: and why, despite a lot of the fear and our anxiety and our discomfort, this experience is totally normal.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么尽管有很多恐惧、焦虑和不安，这种经历其实是非常正常的。

sentences.en: It's natural, and it's going to be okay.
sentences.zh: 这是自然的，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: Every one of us has had to witness as someone they were once really close to slowly kind of drips away, replies to their messages less and less,
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都曾眼睁睁看着曾经非常亲密的人慢慢疏远，回复消息越来越少，

sentences.en: finds new friends who are maybe better for them whilst you're, you know, left feeling a little bit discarded, a little bit unmoored, or maybe you are the friend who has moved on
sentences.zh: 找到可能更适合他们的新朋友，而你却感到被抛弃、无所适从，或者也许你就是那个已经向前看的朋友，

sentences.en: and you're coming to terms with the realization that you have outgrown the people who were once your closest friends.
sentences.zh: 你正在接受一个事实，那就是你已经超越了曾经最亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: The friendship group has disbanded, your friend's just got a new partner.
sentences.zh: 朋友圈解散了，你的朋友刚有了新伴侣。

sentences.en: There are so many ways that we see our friendships change.
sentences.zh: 我们看到友谊发生变化的方式有很多种。

sentences.en: And it's scary because those relationships are really what hold us up during this decade as we slowly kind of separate away from the security of the family unit,
sentences.zh: 这很可怕，因为在20多岁这个十年里，当我们慢慢脱离家庭的保护伞，

sentences.en: and we're trying to form our own identity.
sentences.zh: 试图建立自己的身份时，这些关系确实是支撑我们的支柱。

sentences.en: Having a broad set of friends in those moments to really rely on and call upon is super vital.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻拥有一个可以依靠和求助的广泛朋友圈是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And it's also really vital for our mental health.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的心理健康也至关重要。

sentences.en: There's been so many studies that have shown that people who have close friends, close confidants, they're more satisfied with their lives,
sentences.zh: 有许多研究表明，拥有亲密朋友和知己的人，对生活的满意度更高，

sentences.en: they're less likely to suffer from depression.
sentences.zh: 他们患抑郁症的可能性更小。

sentences.en: They overall just feel happier.
sentences.zh: 他们总体上感觉更快乐。

sentences.en: And in contrast, people with poor quality friendships or no friends, they are twice as likely to die prematurely.
sentences.zh: 相反，那些友谊质量差或没有朋友的人，过早死亡的可能性是前者的两倍。

sentences.en: Of course, they suffer increased loneliness.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也会遭受更严重的孤独感。

sentences.en: So maintaining a really healthy, broad, fulfilling network of friendships is undoubtedly important.
sentences.zh: 因此，维持一个健康、广泛且充实的友谊网络无疑是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And it's not just about the fact that they provide us with comfort and are obviously massive contributors to our health, but friendship is also just one
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为它们为我们提供安慰，显然也是我们健康的重要贡献者，而且友谊本身也是，

sentences.en: of the greatest joys in life, right?
sentences.zh: 人生最大的乐趣之一，对吧？

sentences.en: There are genuinely friends I consider family who know more about me than any partner of mine ever has who make me laugh like beyond reason.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些朋友被我视为家人，他们比我任何伴侣都更了解我，他们能让我毫无理由地开怀大笑。

sentences.en: That connection is so deep that we never want it to fade.
sentences.zh: 那种联系如此深厚，以至于我们从不希望它消逝。

sentences.en: In fact, I think we never consider the fact that it might, it might, it will.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为我们从未考虑过它可能会消逝，它可能会，它终究会。

sentences.en: That is not where our brain naturally goes to the conclusion of the friendship.
sentences.zh: 那并不是我们大脑自然会想到的友谊的终点。

sentences.en: Because unlike romantic relationships, I think friendships aren't meant to have an expiry date.
sentences.zh: 因为与浪漫关系不同，我认为友谊不应该有保质期。

sentences.en: They aren't meant to go up in flames.
sentences.zh: 它们不应该以破裂告终。

sentences.en: There isn't meant to be a breakup.
sentences.zh: 不应该有分手这回事。

sentences.en: We're not meant to fall out of love with our friends.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该与朋友不再相爱。

sentences.en: That is kind of the beauty of platonic intimacy and connection.
sentences.zh: 这正是柏拉图式亲密关系和连接的美妙之处。

sentences.en: It's meant to outlast a lot of other forms of love.
sentences.zh: 它注定要比许多其他形式的爱更持久。

sentences.en: So it comes as a shock when we begin to notice our relationships really shifting or drifting apart from people or realising that we have mutually outgrown each other
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们开始注意到我们的关系真的在发生变化，或者与人渐行渐远，或者意识到我们已经互相超越了，

sentences.en: or just need space.
sentences.zh: 或者只是需要空间时，这会让人感到震惊。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time, our instinct is to A, blame ourselves or B, panic.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们的本能是A，责怪自己，或者B，恐慌。

sentences.en: Immediately jump to the worst case scenario.
sentences.zh: 立刻跳到最坏的情况。

sentences.en: What if I lose all my friends and I end up alone?
sentences.zh: 如果我失去了所有的朋友，最后变得孤身一人怎么办？

sentences.en: We don't give ourselves the grace or the permission in these moments of transition to understand that some friendships just have a shorter life cycle
sentences.zh: 在这些转变的时刻，我们没有给自己足够的宽容或许可去理解，有些友谊只是生命周期较短，

sentences.en: and our friendscape is naturally going to shift with age and time.
sentences.zh: 而我们的朋友圈会随着年龄和时间的推移自然发生变化。

sentences.en: And I think that reaction, that entire sequence of events and realisations is what we're really talking about today.
sentences.zh: 我认为那种反应，整个事件和认知的过程，就是我们今天真正要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: Along with all of the psychology that I think comes with watching our friendships change in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 以及我认为伴随着我们20多岁时看着友谊发生变化而产生的所有心理活动。

sentences.en: We are going to explore the why, including the literal scientific formula for friendship, the types of friendship endings from the fizzle to the replacement or the breakup,
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨原因，包括友谊的科学公式，友谊结束的类型，从逐渐疏远到被取代或彻底决裂，

sentences.en: how intensity may actually shorten the lifespan of our friendships and the impact of simply just entering into a new chapter of your life and dealing with some of the loneliness
sentences.zh: 强度实际上可能会缩短友谊的寿命，以及进入人生新阶段并应对随之而来的孤独感的影响，

sentences.en: that might come along with that.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们要讨论的。

sentences.en: I think there are a lot of friendship misconceptions that keep us stuck in really, really draining relationships.
sentences.zh: 我认为有很多关于友谊的误解，让我们陷入了非常、非常令人心力交瘁的关系中。

sentences.en: You know, am I a bad person if I don't want to be friends with this person anymore?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我不想再和这个人做朋友，我是个坏人吗？

sentences.en: Am I toxic because all of my friends have kind of moved away and stopped talking to me?
sentences.zh: 因为我所有的朋友都搬走了，不再和我说话，我是不是有毒？

sentences.en: Am I boring?
sentences.zh: 我很无聊吗？

sentences.en: How am I going to adapt to this new reality?
sentences.zh: 我该如何适应这个新的现实？

sentences.en: There is so much to discuss here, especially since I think it is so universal.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多值得讨论的地方，尤其是因为我认为这非常普遍。

sentences.en: It is such an important experience to explore because it is inherently isolating.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的探索经历，因为它本质上是孤立的。

sentences.en: So we don't find ourselves talking about it enough, which is to say in the midst of a massive friendship transition that I'm sure we are all experiencing,
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现自己谈论得不够多，也就是说，在大家都经历着巨大的友谊转变的过程中，

sentences.en: I really hope this helps you.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望这能对你有所帮助。

sentences.en: I hope that this gives you a sense of guidance.
sentences.zh: 我希望这能给你一种指引感。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the psychology behind why our friendships change and why that is totally okay.
sentences.zh: 那么废话不多说，让我们进入友谊为何会改变以及为什么这完全没问题的心理学分析。

sentences.en: This past year for me has been a period of like rapid transition.
sentences.zh: 过去这一年对我来说是一个快速转变的时期。

sentences.en: And with that, there's been this real shift in who I spend my time with, the friendships I have.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是，我花时间相处的人，我拥有的友谊，都发生了真正的转变。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, it's required a lot of reflecting on some of the people that I've seen fade away from my life and kind of feeling a little bit like
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这需要对一些我看着从我生活中淡出的人进行大量的反思，并且感觉有点像，

sentences.en: my friendship circle is unbalanced.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友圈失衡了。

sentences.en: The two biggest factors for me, I think in that change has been firstly, seeing a lot of my friends move away from the city where we kind of all grew to knew each other
sentences.zh: 我认为这种变化中最大的两个因素是，首先，看到很多朋友搬离了我们当初在大学时，

sentences.en: when we were at university.
sentences.zh: 大家一起成长并相识的城市。

sentences.en: We all went to university at Canberra and I was talking to my boyfriend about this the other day, but I think the reason
sentences.zh: 我们都在堪培拉上了大学，前几天我和男朋友谈到这个，但我认为我感到非常孤立的原因是，

sentences.en: I've been feeling really isolated is because as we like enter into our, I think early and mid twenties in particular, a lot of people choose to scatter.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入20多岁，特别是20多岁出头和中期时，很多人选择四散而去。

sentences.en: A lot of people move away.
sentences.zh: 很多人搬走了。

sentences.en: And of the people that I'm closest to, one now lives in Paris, one lives in London, one lives in Tasmania, which is like a kind of semi-regional island off of Australia.
sentences.zh: 在我最亲近的人中，一个现在住在巴黎，一个住在伦敦，一个住在塔斯马尼亚，那是一个离澳大利亚本土不远的半区域性岛屿。

sentences.en: You know, one of them is in Nepal and everyone just makes the decision that's best for them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中一个在尼泊尔，每个人都做出了最适合自己的决定。

sentences.en: They move on with their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们继续过自己的生活。

sentences.en: And that means that each of us is feeling, I think, uniquely very isolated.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们每个人都感到，我认为，独特地非常孤立。

sentences.en: That distance is naturally going to change kind of the dynamic because you don't have that same proximity and the ease or access to this other person.
sentences.zh: 这种距离自然会改变那种动态，因为你不再拥有同样的亲近感，也不再有接触对方的便利性。

sentences.en: It requires more of an investment.
sentences.zh: 这需要更多的投入。

sentences.en: And if you're not willing to keep that up, you have to be willing to see that friendship
sentences.zh: 如果你不愿意维持下去，你就必须愿意看到那段友谊，

sentences.en: fizzle out a little bit, not be what it once was or kind of hope that they return.
sentences.zh: 稍微淡化一点，不再是曾经的样子，或者希望他们能回来。

sentences.en: And it's one of those magical moments where it's kind of right back to normal.
sentences.zh: 这是一种神奇的时刻，一切又恢复了正常。

sentences.en: So I think that's like the first big change
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是我在个人生活中看到的第一个重大变化。

sentences.en: I've seen in my personal life.
sentences.zh: 第二个因素不仅与特定的友谊有关，而且与整个社交方式有关。

sentences.en: The second factor has to do not just with specific friendships, but an entire way of socializing.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们越老，对18、19甚至20岁时与朋友相处的方式就越失去兴趣，

sentences.en: The older we get, I think we lose some of our interest in the ways we used to hang out with our friends when we were 18 or 19 or even 20,
sentences.zh: 特别是与饮酒文化有关的部分。

sentences.en: particularly to do with the drinking culture.
sentences.zh: 我知道对我个人而言，当我在大学时，

sentences.en: I know for me personally that when I was at uni,
sentences.zh: 那是酗酒的中心。

sentences.en: it was like binge drinking central.
sentences.zh: 那是我们社交方式的一部分。

sentences.en: Like that was part of how we socialize.
sentences.zh: 那是我们度过周四、周五、周六晚上的方式。

sentences.en: That was part of how we spent our, you know,
sentences.zh: 心理学中有一种东西叫做“不良行为联结”，我们有时会发现自己被那些处于同样混乱、

sentences.en: Thursday, Friday, Saturday nights.
sentences.zh: 自我毁灭道路上，或者在那个时刻处于同样境地的人所吸引和依附。

sentences.en: It is this thing in psychology called bad behavior bonding where we sometimes find ourselves really attracted and attached to people who are on an equally chaotic
sentences.zh: 然后我们互相纵容。

sentences.en: and self-destructive path or in that same place as us in that moment.
sentences.zh: 但当一个人决定是时候超越那种状态，他们已经成熟到超过了那个阶段时，这就会以牺牲通过那些行为结交的朋友为代价。

sentences.en: And then we enable each other.
sentences.zh: 我想18岁的Gemma听到这个会很震惊，你知道，我真的不再去夜店了。

sentences.en: But when one person decides it's kind of time to outgrow that, that they've matured past that kind of chapter, it comes at the cost of the friends
sentences.zh: 我真的不想在工作日的晚上熬到凌晨2点。

sentences.en: they made through those behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我想睡觉。

sentences.en: on a weeknight.
sentences.zh: 其中一些显然是环境因素，但也有一些纯粹是心理和个人因素。

sentences.en: I want to be in bed.
sentences.zh: 就像，那不再是我真正感兴趣的事情了。

sentences.en: I want to be watching Seinfeld.
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一个因素，就是我遇到了某个人，我现在有了伴侣。

sentences.en: My threshold for social interaction, and I think most people's threshold for social interaction, has lowered significantly as I've entered like my mid-20s.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入一段关系时，我们社交宇宙、情感宇宙或太阳系的中心，会从我们的友谊转向我们的伴侣。

sentences.en: Some of that is obviously environmental, but also some of it is just psychological and personal.
sentences.zh: 如果你不小心，你就会脱离周围人的轨道。

sentences.en: Like, that's not what I'm really interested in anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你想和你爱上的这个人尽可能多地待在一起。

sentences.en: And then there's the other factor of the fact that I have met someone that I have a partner now.
sentences.zh: 你想一直见到他们。

sentences.en: When we enter into a relationship, the center of our social universe, our emotional universe or solar system, it shifts away from our friendships and towards our partner.
sentences.zh: 你想邀请他们参加你正在做的所有事情。

sentences.en: And if you're not careful, you kind of fall out of orbit with those around you.
sentences.zh: 这有时会以牺牲那些你维持的时间比认识这个人长得多的柏拉图式关系为代价。

sentences.en: You know, you want to spend as much time as possible with this person that you're falling in love with.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为正是这二到三个平行的变化，让我感到相当孤立，也许觉得我没有像我本可以的那样，

sentences.en: You want to see them all the time.
sentences.zh: 快速适应这些情况。

sentences.en: You want to invite them to everything that you're doing.
sentences.zh: 然而，我也认识到，在20多岁时，我们正在乘坐我称之为“友谊过山车”的东西。

sentences.en: That can sometimes come at the expense of those platonic relationships that you've maintained for much longer than you've known this person.
sentences.zh: “友谊过山车”是我注意到的这种现象，

sentences.en: So I think it's these, like, two to three parallel changes that have left me feeling pretty isolated, perhaps feeling like I haven't adapted as quickly to these situations
sentences.zh: 即我们有一天会因为友谊而感到无比快乐和满足，几乎被爱淹没，你知道。

sentences.en: as I could have.
sentences.zh: 然后三天后，你可能会陷入这种完全的，

sentences.en: However, I also recognize that in our 20s, we are riding what I like to call the friendship rollercoaster.
sentences.zh: 思想螺旋，关于我们如何一无所有，我们如何完全孤独，没有人想和我们一起花时间。

sentences.en: The friendship rollercoaster is this phenomenon
sentences.zh: 友谊过山车就是这样一种现象

sentences.en: I've noticed whereby we can feel incredibly happy and fulfilled by our friendships, almost overwhelmed with love, you know, one day.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，我们有时会因为友谊而感到无比快乐和满足，甚至被爱意淹没，你知道的，就在某一天。

sentences.en: And then three days later, you can end up in this total
sentences.zh: 然后三天后，你又会陷入一种彻底的

sentences.en: thought spiral about how we have no one, how we're totally alone, how no one wants to spend time as, you know, with us.
sentences.zh: 思维漩涡，觉得自己一无所有，觉得自己孤身一人，觉得根本没人想和我们待在一起。

sentences.en: As if three days earlier, you hadn't been having the best time.
sentences.zh: 就好像三天前，你明明还过得非常开心。

sentences.en: You hadn't been feeling totally validated.
sentences.zh: 你明明还感觉自己完全得到了认可。

sentences.en: That is the friendship rollercoaster of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们二十多岁时友谊的过山车。

sentences.en: There are a lot of really high highs and a lot of really low lows.
sentences.zh: 会有很多非常高光的时刻，也会有很多非常低谷的时刻。

sentences.en: And normally at those low points, nothing really has changed except our mental state.
sentences.zh: 通常在那些低谷期，除了我们的心理状态，其实什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: And it goes to show how so much of our experience of feeling isolated or lonely is entirely subjective and it's based on what I think is a very instinctual inherent fear
sentences.zh: 这说明我们感到孤立或孤独的体验，很大程度上是完全主观的，而且我认为这是基于一种非常本能的、与生俱来的恐惧，

sentences.en: of loneliness that is not always based on the truth.
sentences.zh: 一种并不总是基于事实的对孤独的恐惧。

sentences.en: It is a false alarm.
sentences.zh: 这是一种虚假的警报。

sentences.en: That is why we are so fearful of our friendships changing because underneath that fear is a much more primal fear of being alone.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们如此害怕友谊发生变化，因为在这种恐惧之下，隐藏着一种更原始的对孤独的恐惧。

sentences.en: And so we become really hypervigilant to any cues, small suggestions
sentences.zh: 所以我们变得对任何细微的迹象、微小的暗示都高度警惕，

sentences.en: that, you know, point to the fact that our relationships are weakening, that people are becoming more distant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些指向我们的关系正在变淡、人们正在变得疏远的迹象。

sentences.en: Sometimes that is true.
sentences.zh: 有时确实如此。

sentences.en: As sad as it is, we are naturally going to lose friends.
sentences.zh: 虽然很令人难过，但我们自然会失去一些朋友。

sentences.en: It is unavoidable.
sentences.zh: 这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about why we see that so often in our 20s in particular.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈为什么我们在二十多岁时会如此频繁地看到这种情况。

sentences.en: this decade is a period of transition for all of us.
sentences.zh: 这十年对我们所有人来说都是一个过渡期。

sentences.en: Career transition, mental transition, emotional transition, even physical transition as we've spoken about as we kind of move, we scatter, we pursue different paths.
sentences.zh: 职业转型、心理转型、情感转型，甚至是我们之前提到过的身体上的转型，随着我们搬迁、分散、追求不同的道路。

sentences.en: Everyone is kind of on their own, you know, I know it sounds cheesy, but their own journey in that moment.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在经历着，我知道这听起来很老套，但每个人在那一刻确实都在经历着属于自己的旅程。

sentences.en: We are all trying equally as hard as everyone else to just figure out what we want from life and how we can actually do those things.
sentences.zh: 我们都在同样努力地去弄清楚我们想要什么样的生活，以及我们如何才能真正实现这些目标。

sentences.en: It's interesting because I think although we are all the same age, we are all almost at like different life points.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我认为虽然我们年龄相仿，但我们几乎处于不同的人生阶段。

sentences.en: We've all hit different milestones.
sentences.zh: 我们都达到了不同的里程碑。

sentences.en: Some of us are still living at home.
sentences.zh: 有些人还住在家里。

sentences.en: Some of us have moved in with like partners.
sentences.zh: 有些人已经和伴侣同居了。

sentences.en: We're living abroad.
sentences.zh: 我们住在国外。

sentences.en: Some of us are still at uni.
sentences.zh: 有些人还在上大学。

sentences.en: We are all at these very different stages, whereas for the first
sentences.zh: 我们都处于这些非常不同的阶段，而在我们生命的前

sentences.en: 18 years of our lives, if someone was our age, we could assume that they were doing a lot of the same things as we were.
sentences.zh: 18年里，如果有人和我们同龄，我们可以假设他们正在做很多和我们一样的事情。

sentences.en: We were kind of living parallel lives because of the structures of childhood and adolescence.
sentences.zh: 由于童年和青春期的结构，我们过着某种平行的生活。

sentences.en: But in our 20s, that all splinters.
sentences.zh: 但在二十多岁时，这一切都分崩离析了。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a life path explosion.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一场人生道路的爆炸。

sentences.en: It's at this point of, I don't want to say, you know, upheaval, but like significant growth and impact that we see the relationships around us change as well.
sentences.zh: 正是在这种，我不想说是动荡，但可以说是重大成长和影响的时刻，我们看到周围的关系也发生了变化。

sentences.en: And they will continue to do so for the remainder of our 20s and the remainder of our lives.
sentences.zh: 而且在我们的二十多岁余下的时间里，以及我们余生中，这种情况还会继续发生。

sentences.en: One of the biggest moments that I think we encounter this is following university or high school.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们遇到这种情况最大的时刻之一是在大学或高中毕业之后。

sentences.en: When we are at uni, we spend so much time together.
sentences.zh: 当我们上大学时，我们花很多时间在一起。

sentences.en: There is just endless opportunities to be around your friends, opportunities to laugh, to have fun.
sentences.zh: 有无穷无尽的机会和朋友在一起，有机会欢笑，有机会玩乐。

sentences.en: And we are having this very shared experience.
sentences.zh: 我们正在经历这种非常共同的体验。

sentences.en: We're working towards the same goal to, you know, graduate at the end of all this.
sentences.zh: 我们朝着同一个目标努力，你知道，在这一切结束时毕业。

sentences.en: And our friendships at that point are really, really convenient.
sentences.zh: 那时我们的友谊真的非常非常方便。

sentences.en: You are living in the same place, possibly the same town, even sometimes the same building.
sentences.zh: 你们住在同一个地方，可能在同一个城镇，甚至有时在同一栋楼里。

sentences.en: You're going to the library every day.
sentences.zh: 你们每天都去图书馆。

sentences.en: You are eating together every day, seeing each other as much as you can.
sentences.zh: 你们每天一起吃饭，尽可能多地见面。

sentences.en: And when we no longer have,
sentences.zh: 而当我们不再拥有，

sentences.en: A, those shared experiences or B, the shared environment, we slowly lose that closeness.
sentences.zh: A，那些共同的经历，或者B，共同的环境，我们就会慢慢失去那种亲密感。

sentences.en: And to understand this, we really need to look at the psychological principles underlying friendship.
sentences.zh: 为了理解这一点，我们真的需要看看友谊背后的心理学原则。

sentences.en: These researchers back in the 90s, they proposed that there are four key ingredients or factors that can basically predict whether you and someone else will become friends
sentences.zh: 这些研究人员在90年代提出，有四个关键要素或因素，基本上可以预测你和某人是否会成为朋友，

sentences.en: and also whether you'll be able to maintain that friendship.
sentences.zh: 以及你是否能够维持那段友谊。

sentences.en: And these, like, ingredients are proximity, similarity, familiarity, and reciprocity.
sentences.zh: 这些要素是：邻近性、相似性、熟悉度和互惠性。

sentences.en: So, proximity basically just means physical closeness.
sentences.zh: 邻近性基本上就是指身体上的接近。

sentences.en: How easy is it for you to see this person regularly?
sentences.zh: 你定期见到这个人的难易程度如何？

sentences.en: They did a study on this at university dorm rooms and they found that how close people's rooms were to each other actually predicted the likelihood of them becoming friends.
sentences.zh: 他们在大学宿舍里做过一项研究，发现人们房间之间的距离实际上预测了他们成为朋友的可能性。

sentences.en: A lot of our friendships basically come down to the ease of contact and the frequency of contact.
sentences.zh: 我们很多友谊基本上归结为接触的便利性和接触的频率。

sentences.en: Secondly, we have similarity.
sentences.zh: 其次是相似性。

sentences.en: We're obviously going to like someone more if they share the same interests, hobbies, lifestyle, beliefs as us.
sentences.zh: 如果对方和我们有相同的兴趣、爱好、生活方式和信仰，我们显然会更喜欢他们。

sentences.en: But this also includes similarity in terms of current and past life experiences or a similar, sharing a similar environment.
sentences.zh: 但这还包括在当前和过去的生活经历方面的相似性，或者分享相似的环境。

sentences.en: Then we have familiarity that refers to not just how long we've known someone, how close we are with them, but also the depth of the connection.
sentences.zh: 然后是熟悉度，这不仅指我们认识某人多久，我们和他们有多亲近，还指联系的深度。

sentences.en: You know, sometimes we think that the people who have known us the longest know us the beSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时我们认为认识我们最久的人最了解我们。

sentences.en: That is not always the case.
sentences.zh: 事实并非总是如此。

sentences.en: Sometimes we meet people and there is just this intense, intense spark, this intense platonic chemistry such that we automatically, immediately feel like we have known them
sentences.zh: 有时我们遇到一些人，会产生一种强烈的、强烈的火花，这种强烈的柏拉图式化学反应，让我们自动地、立即地感觉好像我们已经认识他们

sentences.en: our whole lives.
sentences.zh: 一辈子了。

sentences.en: Familiarity is basically just close knowledge of another person.
sentences.zh: 熟悉度基本上就是对另一个人有深入的了解。

sentences.en: And finally, we have reciprocity, which is knowing that what you give someone in terms of your love, in terms of your energy, in terms of your time, is going to be returned,
sentences.zh: 最后是互惠性，即知道你在爱、精力、时间方面给予某人的东西，将会得到回报，

sentences.en: is going to be reciprocated.
sentences.zh: 将会得到回应。

sentences.en: So those are the most important factors.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是最重要的因素。

sentences.en: When we talk about our friendships changing in our 20s,
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论二十多岁时友谊的变化时，

sentences.en: 9 out of 10 times I would say that change normally comes down to a shift in one of these four conditions.
sentences.zh: 十有八九我会说，这种变化通常归结为这四个条件中某一个的改变。

sentences.en: for example, when people move away or they get really busy, they start full-time work, we lose that proximity.
sentences.zh: 例如，当人们搬走或变得非常忙碌，开始全职工作时，我们就失去了那种邻近性。

sentences.en: It makes it harder to see them.
sentences.zh: 这使得见到他们变得更难了。

sentences.en: When we lose those shared experiences, like no longer being at university together, we have less to talk about.
sentences.zh: 当我们失去那些共同的经历，比如不再一起上大学时，我们可谈的话题就少了。

sentences.en: When we lose that familiarity, we feel like this person no longer knows us.
sentences.zh: 当我们失去那种熟悉感时，我们会觉得这个人不再了解我们了。

sentences.en: And when we begin to see a friendship as one-sided without that reciprocity we were speaking about, this is when it makes us question how much this person really wants us to be in
sentences.zh: 当我们开始认为一段友谊是单方面的，没有我们刚才谈到的那种互惠性时，这就会让我们质疑这个人到底有多想让我们出现在

sentences.en: their life.
sentences.zh: 他们的生活中。

sentences.en: What I often say is that friendships can survive a reduction or a change in one of these conditions, but not to.
sentences.zh: 我常说，友谊可以在其中一个条件减少或改变的情况下存续，但不能同时失去两个。

sentences.en: So, for example, it's totally fine if your friend gets really busy at work and can only see you once a fortnight, once a month, as long as you maintain that similarity,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，如果你的朋友工作变得非常忙，两周或一个月只能见你一次，这完全没问题，只要你们保持那种相似性、

sentences.en: familiarity, reciprocity.
sentences.zh: 熟悉度和互惠性。

sentences.en: You make time when you have time and you talk about things that are interesting and you want to see them.
sentences.zh: 你有时间的时候会腾出时间，你们谈论有趣的事情，并且你们都想见到对方。

sentences.en: But if suddenly you no longer have those shared stories, beliefs, values, interests, and then you also don't see them regularly, that is when the friendship starts to crumble.
sentences.zh: 但如果突然间你们不再有那些共同的故事、信仰、价值观、兴趣，而且你们也不再经常见面，那友谊就开始瓦解了。

sentences.en: Or if the friend is not reciprocating your excitement or your investment in seeing them, again we really begin to question the value of the friendship or how much longer it
sentences.zh: 或者如果朋友没有回应你的兴奋或你在见面上的投入，我们再次开始真正质疑这段友谊的价值，或者它还能持续

sentences.en: can laSt.
sentences.zh: 多久。

sentences.en: I want to stress this again, I know that that feels really painful, but it's not abnormal.
sentences.zh: 我想再次强调这一点，我知道这感觉非常痛苦，但这并不反常。

sentences.en: You are not the only one who is either going through these changes themselves, struggling to connect with people you once loved, or watching someone else feel the same way about
sentences.zh: 你不是唯一一个正在经历这些变化的人，不是唯一一个在努力与曾经深爱的人保持联系的人，也不是唯一一个看着别人对

sentences.en: your friendship, watching the people around you suddenly almost disappear.
sentences.zh: 你的友谊有同样感觉的人，看着周围的人突然几乎消失。

sentences.en: Friendships change because people change and sometimes they just don't change in the same direction.
sentences.zh: 友谊会改变是因为人会改变，有时他们只是没有朝着同一个方向改变。

sentences.en: That is not a crime, it is not because there is something wrong with you or something wrong with them.
sentences.zh: 这不是犯罪，不是因为你有什么问题，也不是因为他们有什么问题。

sentences.en: I think the worst thing we can do in response to that is actually act from a place of anger or rejection because you're not actually angry at them, you're just hurt, you're just
sentences.zh: 我认为在应对这种情况时，我们能做的最糟糕的事情就是出于愤怒或拒绝的心态行事，因为你并不是真的对他们生气，你只是受伤了，你只是

sentences.en: scared of losing them, you're just scared of change and your sadness and your panic is in itself an indicator that you love them deeply.
sentences.zh: 害怕失去他们，你只是害怕改变，你的悲伤和恐慌本身就表明你深深地爱着他们。

sentences.en: So I think when we are in those moments where we are really fearful that we're losing people, feeling like we should push them away or, you know, sometimes find a replacement, we
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，当我们处于那些真正害怕失去朋友的时刻，感觉应该把他们推开，或者，你知道，有时想找个替代者时，我们

sentences.en: do just need to pause and approach this very rationally.
sentences.zh: 确实需要停下来，非常理性地对待这件事。

sentences.en: This is all about a transition, it's all about a journey and where you are at now with your friends, like we said, it is the friendship roller coaster, it may not be where you end
sentences.zh: 这一切都是关于过渡，都是关于旅程，就像我们说的，你现在和朋友们所处的位置是友谊的过山车，这可能不是你最终

sentences.en: up.
sentences.zh: 停留的地方。

sentences.en: There are factors as well that I think also alter our friendships
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一些因素也会不可逆转地改变我们的友谊，

sentences.en: irreversibly and that includes really significant events like a big breach of trust, a betrayal,
sentences.zh: 包括非常重大的事件，比如严重的信任破裂、背叛、

sentences.en: misunderstandings, I think these things differ from what we were talking about before and when we encounter those things there are four kind of friendship breakups that we
sentences.zh: 误解，我认为这些事情与我们之前谈论的不同，当我们遇到这些事情时，有四种我们最常看到的友谊破裂。

sentences.en: most often see.
sentences.zh: 这些是友谊的逐渐淡化、替代、单方面的断绝，以及需要采取极端措施的破裂。

sentences.en: These are the friendship fizzle, the replacement, the one-sided severance and the breakup where really drastic measures are required.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，如果我们审视一下我们的友谊，那些来自过去的友谊，相互的逐渐淡化是最常见的。

sentences.en: So I would say if we have a look at our friendships, the mutual and you know friendships from the past, the mutual fizzle is most common.
sentences.zh: 有些人注定不会陪伴我们一生，他们注定只能陪伴我们一段时光。

sentences.en: There are some people we are not meant to be around our entire lives, we are only meant to be with them for a season.
sentences.zh: 在我们需要继续前行之前。

sentences.en: Before it is, you know, time for us to move on.
sentences.zh: 也许这个人只是不再像以前那样填补你的内心了，你们曾经在工作中是朋友，现在你们没有共同的话题可以讨论了，他们是你前任的朋友。

sentences.en: Maybe this person just no longer fills your cup in the same way you were friends at work, now you no longer have that shared topic to discuss, they were your ex's friends.
sentences.zh: 但这里的关键词是相互的。

sentences.en: The key word though here is mutual.
sentences.zh: 我们都明白我们不再像以前那样亲密了，我们周围的环境已经改变了，也许是时候真正放手让对方离开，停止尝试

sentences.en: We both kind of understand that we aren't as close as we once were, the context around us has changed and perhaps it's time to actually just let the other person go, stop trying to
sentences.zh: 重新安排计划，就让它顺其自然地淡化吧。

sentences.en: reschedule the plans, just let it fizzle.

sentences.zh: 此外，即使在害怕的时候也要对事物说“是”，对邀请、活动、加入体育俱乐部、新爱好说“是”。

sentences.en: Take on the philosophy that everyone wants to be your friend.
sentences.zh: 采取一种“每个人都想成为你的朋友”的哲学。

sentences.en: You are magnetic.
sentences.zh: 你很有吸引力。

sentences.en: You attract really good people.
sentences.zh: 你吸引的都是非常好的人。

sentences.en: Don't isolate yourself by thinking that you can only be friends with one type of person or that the length of time you've been friends with someone is the only factor in
sentences.zh: 不要因为认为自己只能与一种人做朋友，或者认为与某人做朋友的时间长短是衡量

sentences.en: your closeness, is the only kind of indicator of compatibility.
sentences.zh: 亲密程度的唯一因素、是兼容性的唯一指标，而将自己孤立起来。

sentences.en: I think that we buy into that a lot.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们很多人都相信这一点。

sentences.en: That just because we've known someone the longest must mean that they are our best friend.
sentences.zh: 认为仅仅因为我们认识某人最久，就一定意味着他们是我们最好的朋友。

sentences.en: And time and time again we see that that is not true.
sentences.zh: 但我们一次又一次地看到，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: That compatibility and chemistry and love and platonic intimacy work in really strange and surprising ways.
sentences.zh: 兼容性、化学反应、爱和柏拉图式的亲密关系以非常奇怪和令人惊讶的方式运作。

sentences.en: And with that, do not buy into this idea that you are past your friendship prime.
sentences.zh: 因此，不要相信你已经过了友谊黄金期的想法。

sentences.en: Because when you believe that there was a time and a place to make your lifelong friends, you've missed it, you've missed the boat, you're subconsciously going
sentences.zh: 因为当你相信结交终身朋友有时机和地点，而你已经错过了它、错过了机会时，你潜意识里

sentences.en: to be less likely to initiate new conversations, new connections, new relationships because you already feel like you've loSt.
sentences.zh: 就不太可能去发起新的对话、建立新的连接、开启新的关系，因为你已经觉得你输了。

sentences.en: You already feel like you're behind.
sentences.zh: 你已经觉得你落后了。

sentences.en: I also think it's very important to not respond with fear when we feel our kind of friendship landscape shifting because fear will have you reacting in ways
sentences.zh: 我还认为，当我们感觉到友谊的格局发生变化时，不要以恐惧来回应是非常重要的，因为恐惧会让你做出

sentences.en: that are irrational and actually counter to your true intentions, which is to foster deep love with those around you, to feel like you belong.
sentences.zh: 非理性的反应，实际上与你的真实意图背道而驰，你的真实意图是与周围的人培养深厚的爱，感到归属感。

sentences.en: Perceived rejection can really sting, but just because your relationship has changed doesn't mean that it needs to be completely discarded.
sentences.zh: 感知的拒绝确实会让人痛苦，但仅仅因为你们的关系发生了变化，并不意味着它需要被完全抛弃。

sentences.en: I think about my friendships at least a lot of the time in terms of levels.
sentences.zh: 我至少在很多时候是根据层级来思考我的友谊的。

sentences.en: You have your top rung, kind of your ride or die friendships, then those friends that you maybe wished you saw more or you're slightly less close to at the moment.
sentences.zh: 你有最顶层的、那种生死之交的友谊，然后是那些你可能希望多见见，或者目前稍微没那么亲近的朋友。

sentences.en: You've got your work friends, you've got your acquaintances who you would very kindly have a chat with in the street and know a little bit about their life, but you're not
sentences.zh: 你有工作上的朋友，有熟人，你会很友好地在街上和他们聊天，了解一点他们的生活，但你并不

sentences.en: super close to.
sentences.zh: 特别亲近。

sentences.en: And then you have strangers.
sentences.zh: 然后是陌生人。

sentences.en: Maybe this person, this person that you were thinking about right now, this friend, is just sitting at a rung lower than normal.
sentences.zh: 也许这个人，你现在正在想的这个人，这个朋友，只是处于比平时低一级的层级上。

sentences.en: Does that mean that they need to be completely relegated to the strangers category?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着他们需要被完全归入陌生人类别？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能不是。

sentences.en: They're just at a different point in their relationship to you.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在与你的关系中处于不同的阶段。

sentences.en: But you should keep the door open for them to come back in, for them to promote themselves back up to top rung.
sentences.zh: 但你应该为他们敞开大门，让他们回来，让他们重新晋升到顶层。

sentences.en: Obviously, this does not apply to friends who have totally crossed boundaries with you or who have treated you terribly, but just those who have maybe just have different
sentences.zh: 显然，这不适用于那些完全越界或对待你非常糟糕的朋友，只适用于那些可能只是有不同

sentences.en: priorities right now.
sentences.zh: 优先事项的人。

sentences.en: Give them the grace that you would want in that situation.
sentences.zh: 给予他们你在那种情况下会希望得到的宽容。

sentences.en: So I actually have a story about this.
sentences.zh: 所以我其实有一个关于这个的故事。

sentences.en: I have a very, very close friend of mine, possibly my longest friend, and we were incredibly close for the first three or four years that we after we'd met.
sentences.zh: 我有一个非常非常亲密的朋友，可能是认识时间最长的朋友，我们在认识后的前三四年里非常亲密。

sentences.en: Like we did everything together.
sentences.zh: 我们凡事都一起做。

sentences.en: We knew everything about each other's life.
sentences.zh: 我们了解彼此生活中的一切。

sentences.en: And then we went through this period almost randomly without any context of just like complete disconnect.
sentences.zh: 然后我们经历了一段几乎是随机的、没有任何背景的完全断联的时期。

sentences.en: We saw each other rarely.
sentences.zh: 我们很少见面。

sentences.en: I really did feel like for certain that the friendship was over.
sentences.zh: 我确实确信这段友谊已经结束了。

sentences.en: It was really upsetting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人难过。

sentences.en: It weighed really heavily on my mind, but I didn't want to close the door.
sentences.zh: 它沉重地压在我的心头，但我不想关上那扇门。

sentences.en: And I know that she didn't want to either.
sentences.zh: 我知道她也不想。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, two years on, I think even a little bit longer than that now, like three or four years on, we are back to that same level of closeness, maybe even closer.
sentences.zh: 结果呢，两年后，我想现在甚至更久一点了，大概三四年后，我们又回到了同样的亲密程度，甚至可能更亲密。

sentences.en: She is one of the best people in my life.
sentences.zh: 她是我生命中最棒的人之一。

sentences.en: And I think it's because we gave each other permission, maybe even subconsciously to follow our own paths that our friendship has allowed to, you know, is allowed to be this
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为我们给了彼此许可，甚至可能是潜意识里的，去追随我们自己的道路，这让我们的友谊能够，你知道，能够变得如此

sentences.en: strong because we've seen it through moments of tension and moments of change.
sentences.zh: 坚固，因为我们一起经历了紧张和变化的时刻。

sentences.en: And we knew that either we would come back to each other or we wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，要么我们会回到彼此身边，要么不会。

sentences.en: And we would still be incredibly happy for the other person.
sentences.zh: 而我们仍然会为对方感到无比高兴。

sentences.en: Change does not mean death.
sentences.zh: 变化并不意味着死亡。

sentences.en: It does not mean the end.
sentences.zh: 它并不意味着终结。

sentences.en: The best kinds of friendships change and evolve despite factors like time and proximity.
sentences.zh: 最好的友谊会随着时间、距离等因素而改变和演变。

sentences.en: Don't panic.
sentences.zh: 不要惊慌。

sentences.en: I promise the fear you have is temporary.
sentences.zh: 我保证你感到的恐惧是暂时的。

sentences.en: And alongside that, that fear may also motivate you to make new friends, to go out there and, I don't know, actually put yourself in a position that you haven't had to before.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这种恐惧也可能激励你去结交新朋友，走出去，我不知道，真正把自己置于一个你以前不必置身的境地。

sentences.en: Put yourself in a position where friendship isn't as convenient and at once as it once was.
sentences.zh: 把自己置于一个友谊不像以前那样方便的境地。

sentences.en: But now you have, you know, the opportunity to choose.
sentences.zh: 但现在你有了，你知道，选择的机会。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Someone once said to me, I was asking this person, he was like, I don't really have many friends.
sentences.zh: 有人曾经对我说，我当时问这个人，他说，我真的没有很多朋友。

sentences.en: And I was like, why?
sentences.zh: 我说，为什么？

sentences.en: You know, aren't you lonely?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不孤独吗？

sentences.en: Why don't why wouldn't you want a million friends?
sentences.zh: 为什么，为什么你不想拥有一百万个朋友？

sentences.en: And he was like, well, the people around you are who you become.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，你周围的人决定了你会成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: And so I think that it's actually worthwhile to be a little bit picky when it comes to that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在这一点上稍微挑剔一点是值得的。

sentences.en: And maybe if you are at a place where you are quite isolated and you are, you know, you're quite lonely, you have seen a lot of friendships change.
sentences.zh: 也许如果你处于一个相当孤立、相当孤独的地方，你已经看到很多友谊发生了变化。

sentences.en: Instead of viewing it as this like negative, like life ending thing of like, I'm never going to have what I once had.
sentences.zh: 不要把它看作是一种消极的、像人生终结一样的事情，觉得“我再也不会拥有我曾经拥有的东西了”。

sentences.en: I'm never going to feel connected or like I belong again, view it as a new beginning, be like, wow, I get to like, I get to create the life that I want here.
sentences.zh: “我再也不会感到连接或归属感了”，把它看作是一个新的开始，心想，哇，我可以在这里创造我想要的生活。

sentences.en: I get to make the friendships that I would like to make.
sentences.zh: 我可以结交我想要结交的朋友。

sentences.en: I get to be surprised by the people who are one day just going to walk in the door and completely change who I am.
sentences.zh: 我可以被那些有一天会走进门来并彻底改变我的人所惊喜。

sentences.en: I think loneliness is just an emotion.
sentences.zh: 我认为孤独只是一种情绪。

sentences.en: It is just a message from our mind telling us what we need the same way that hunger tells us, you know, that our body needs fuel or thirst tells us that we need hydration.
sentences.zh: 它只是我们大脑发出的一个信号，告诉我们我们需要什么，就像饥饿告诉我们，你知道，我们的身体需要燃料，或者口渴告诉我们我们需要补水一样。

sentences.en: Loneliness and feeling disconnected to people tells you that it's time to reach out.
sentences.zh: 孤独和感到与人断联是在告诉你，是时候去联系了。

sentences.en: And I guess that's my final tip here.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我最后的建议。

sentences.en: Be honest with your friends that you would like to see them more or you would like to chat more often.
sentences.zh: 对你的朋友诚实，告诉他们你希望多见见他们，或者你希望更频繁地聊天。

sentences.en: I did this the other day with my friend Steph where I was like, I'm on the friendship roller coaster right now and I'm at a dip.
sentences.zh: 我前几天和我的朋友Steph就这样做了，我说，我现在正处于友谊的过山车上，我处于低谷。

sentences.en: Can we make time to see each other?
sentences.zh: 我们能抽出时间见面吗？

sentences.en: And of course she said yes.
sentences.zh: 当然，她答应了。

sentences.en: That openness, that vulnerability is vital here because often others in our life don't really know what we're going through.
sentences.zh: 那种开放、那种脆弱在这里至关重要，因为我们生活中的其他人通常并不知道我们正在经历什么。

sentences.en: They don't know how we're feeling.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道我们的感受。

sentences.en: They may not have noticed what we have noticed that we have drifted.
sentences.zh: 他们可能没有注意到我们所注意到的——我们已经渐行渐远了。

sentences.en: So you can choose to say nothing or you can choose to be honest with how with how you feel in that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以选择什么都不说，或者你可以选择对你那一刻的感受保持诚实。

sentences.en: And 90% of the time the people who truly love you want you to be happy and they will respond positively to that and they will make time for you.
sentences.zh: 90%的情况下，真正爱你的人希望你快乐，他们会对你的诚实做出积极的回应，他们会为你抽出时间。

sentences.en: It is just a matter of of reaching out.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个联系的问题。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: In case I haven't said it enough times, this is not just you.
sentences.zh: 如果我还没说过足够多次的话，这不仅仅是你一个人。

sentences.en: I know it's hard.
sentences.zh: 我知道这很难。

sentences.en: Change is hard.
sentences.zh: 改变很难。

sentences.en: Human beings naturally fear change.
sentences.zh: 人类天生害怕改变。

sentences.en: Isolation is hard.
sentences.zh: 孤独很难。

sentences.en: But do not blame yourself or start to internalize what are actually really common transitions here as a sign that there is something wrong with you or that
sentences.zh: 但不要责怪自己，或者开始将这些实际上非常常见的过渡内化，认为这是你有什么问题，或者

sentences.en: you are undeserving of good, long lasting friendships.
sentences.zh: 你不配拥有美好的、长久的友谊的迹象。

sentences.en: You absolutely are.
sentences.zh: 你绝对配得上。

sentences.en: You just may not have found them yet.
sentences.zh: 你可能只是还没找到他们。

sentences.en: I always think of this quote and it brings me so much peace and kind of these moments of catastrophizing.
sentences.zh: 我总是想起这句话，它带给我很多平静，在这些灾难化的时刻。

sentences.en: You haven't yet met all the people who you will love in this life.
sentences.zh: 你还没有遇到所有你会在这一生中爱的人。

sentences.en: And I think that is so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我认为这太美好了。

sentences.en: How magical is it to imagine all of the people who are now strangers one day being individuals in your life who you won't be able to live without.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，所有现在是陌生人的人，有一天会成为你生命中不可或缺的人，这有多神奇。

sentences.en: These people who you will one day meet who will tell you the story of the life they are now living.
sentences.zh: 这些你有一天会遇到的人，他们会告诉你他们现在正在过的生活的故事。

sentences.en: We are so young.
sentences.zh: 我们还很年轻。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's so impossible to really appreciate how young we are.
sentences.zh: 有时真的很难意识到我们有多年轻。

sentences.en: It is not the end of the road.
sentences.zh: 这并不是路的尽头。

sentences.en: There is so much more love to experience.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的爱等着你去体验。

sentences.en: And like we said, there has been so many studies that have shown that not only is this incredibly common, but a lot of us replace, you know, 50% of our friends,
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，有许多研究表明，这不仅非常普遍，而且我们很多人会更换掉大约50%的朋友，

sentences.en: 80% of our friends every seven years.
sentences.zh: 每七年就会更换掉80%的朋友。

sentences.en: You are just in a transition period right now, along with many, many others, one that you will come out of and you'll be able to look back at and say, I needed that to happen.
sentences.zh: 你现在正处于一个过渡期，和你一样处于这个阶段的人还有很多很多，你会走出来的，回头看时你会说，我当时确实需要经历这一切。

sentences.en: I needed to see these friendships fade away.
sentences.zh: 我需要看着这些友谊逐渐淡去。

sentences.en: I needed to be alone for a while in order to really appreciate how beautiful these new people in my life are.
sentences.zh: 我需要独自待上一段时间，才能真正体会到生命中这些新出现的人是多么美好。

sentences.en: So I really hope that this episode has helped normalize this experience for you.
sentences.zh: 所以我真心希望这一集能让你觉得这种经历是很正常的。

sentences.en: I totally understand the fear.
sentences.zh: 我完全理解这种恐惧。

sentences.en: Please, I feel like I live this fear every day.
sentences.zh: 真的，我觉得我每天都生活在这种恐惧中。

sentences.en: So it was actually quite comforting to discuss this and to kind of explore, I think, some of the reasons behind why we see that happen.
sentences.zh: 所以能讨论这个话题，并探索我们认为导致这种现象发生的一些原因，其实挺让人宽慰的。

sentences.en: I really do hope that you enjoyed this episode.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望你喜欢这一集。

sentences.en: I hope it brought you comfort.
sentences.zh: 希望它能带给你安慰。

sentences.en: As always, if you feel like there is someone in your life who feels this way, who needs to hear this episode, please feel free to send them the link
sentences.zh: 一如既往，如果你觉得你生命中有人也有这种感受，需要听听这一集，请随时把链接发给他们，

sentences.en: to share it along, to share the love along.
sentences.zh: 分享出去，把这份爱传递下去。

sentences.en: Leave a five-star review if you feel called to do so and make sure you're following so that you know when new episodes come out.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，请留下五星好评，并确保关注我们，这样你就能及时收到新一集的更新提醒。

sentences.en: If you have an episode suggestion as well, please follow us at that psychology podcast on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 如果你有关于节目的建议，也请在Instagram上关注我们：that psychology podcast。

sentences.en: I love hearing from you guys.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢听你们分享。

sentences.en: I love hearing about what your 20s has been like.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢听你们讲述自己的二十多岁是什么样的。

sentences.en: You guys always have the most amazing suggestions for topics I have never considered before.
sentences.zh: 你们总是能提出一些我从未考虑过的、非常棒的话题建议。

sentences.en: So follow us over there.
sentences.zh: 所以，去那边关注我们吧。

sentences.en: And as always, we will be back next week with another episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我们下周会带着新的一集回来。

sentences.zh: 这是一档iHeart播客。

sentences.zh: 保证由人类制作。
